KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.claim: Abraham identifies all gods worshipped instead of God as fabricated and their worshippers as misguided; God alone creates, guides, feeds, gives drink, heals, causes death and life, and forgives sins on Judgment Day.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.anchor: gerçek ve tapılmaya lâyık olan tanrının yaratan, hidayete erdiren, yediren, içiren, şifa veren, öldüren, hayat veren ve kıyamet gününde günahları bağışlayan Allah Teâlâ olduğuna dikkat çekmiştir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r4.claim: Eating and drinking are God’s physical provisions; polytheists treated their deities as sources of sustenance even though they did not regard them as creators of the universe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r4.anchor: they in fact regarded them to be a source of blessings and sustenance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.claim: Abraham presents the fundamentals of his preaching in logical order as personal impressions rather than argument, because in the acquittal and migration phase intellectual persuasion is useless; the subtle style may still stir hearts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.anchor: instead of presenting them through arguments and reasoning, he has expressed them in the form of personal impressions.

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r1.claim: The repeated relative pronoun in three clauses shows that each divine attribute independently establishes the Lord's claim.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r1.anchor: وتكرير الموصول في المواقع الثلاثة للدلالة على أن كل واحدة من الصلات مستقلة باقتضاء الحكم

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r2.claim: God alone feeds Abraham whatever food He wills and gives him whatever drink He wills.

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r3.claim: Feeding and giving drink include more than creating and handing over food: God also grants appetite, chewing, swallowing, digestion, and elimination, all needed to benefit from them.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r3.anchor: وليس الإطعام والسقي عبارتين عن مجرد خلق الطعام والشراب له

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra's prayer asks God for a grinding molar, a digesting stomach, and an effective bowel, underscoring the bodily means required to benefit from food.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r4.anchor: ومن دعاء أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه : "اللهم اجعل لي ضرسا طحونا ومعدة هضوما ودبرا بثورا"

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r5.claim: The verse points to trust, contentment, submission, entrusting affairs to God, cutting off reliance on causes, turning fully to Him, and turning away from everything else.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r5.anchor: وأشارت الآية إلى مقام التوكل والرضى والتسليم والتفويض وقطع الأسباب والإقبال إليه بالكلية والإعراض عما سواه

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r6.speaker: صاحب بحر الحقائق
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r6.claim: The author of Baḥr al-Ḥaqāʾiq reads the food as worship that revives hearts and the drink as a holy manifestation of divine lordship that refreshes spirits.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r6.anchor: صاحب "بحر الحقائق" : (فرمودكه مراد طعام عبوديستت كه دلها بآن زنده شود وشراب طهور تجلى صفت ربوبيت

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r7.speaker: ذو النون مصري
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r7.claim: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī says the food is knowledge of God and the drink is love.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r7.anchor: وذو النون مصري قدس سره فرمودكه اين طعام طعام معرفتست واين شراب شراب محبت

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r8.claim: A cited couplet praises love's wine as the best wine and calls every other drink a mirage.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r8.anchor: شراب المحبة خير الشراب وكل شراب سواه سراب

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r9.claim: Bursevī says the prophetic report 'I spend the night with my Lord; He feeds and gives me drink' can be understood from the verse's deeper implication.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r9.anchor: واز فحواي كلام شمه از أسرار كلام حقائق نظام (أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقيني)

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r10.speaker: أحد القولين
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r10.claim: One of two reported opinions takes the prophetic feeding and drinking literally as food and drink for the mouth, noting that this reading preserves the ordinary sense of the words.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أنه طعام وشراب حسي للفم قالوا

BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r11.speaker: القول الثاني
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r11.claim: The other opinion understands the prophetic nourishment as divine knowledge, intimate conversation, nearness, love, and other states that feed hearts and spirits.
BURSEVI:v6p205#2/r11.anchor: والثاني : أن المراد به ما يغذيه الله به من معارفه وما يفيض على قلبه من لذة مناجاته

QIRAAT-ER:26:79:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:79:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:26:79:6#1/r1.claim: The reading restores the first-person yāʾ after yasqīnī; the fuller suffix changes prosodic weight but not meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:26:79:6#1/r1.anchor: no semantic change but alters prosodic weight

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r14.claim: The apparent sense of feeding and giving drink is ordinary food and drink, and Abraham lists these as continuing provisions that sustain life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r14.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: يطعمني ويسقين: الطعام المعروف المعهود، والسقي المعهود، وفيه تعديد نعمة الرزق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r15.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r15.claim: Abū Bakr al-Warrāq interprets the feeding and drink as occurring without food or drink.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r15.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: يطعمني بلا طعام، ويسقيني بلا شراب، كما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r1.claim: Creation needs no emphatic هو because no one can claim it; guidance, feeding, and drinking can be claimed, so their statements emphasize that God alone provides them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r1.anchor: ولما كان الخلق لا يمكن أن يدعيه أحد لم يؤكد فيه بهو، فلم يكن التركيب الذي هو خلقني، ولما كانت الهداية قد يمكن ادعاؤها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r2.claim: After creation and guidance, Abraham names food and drink, the provisions that keep life going; excess or deficiency can upset the body and bring illness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r2.anchor: وذكر بعد نعمة الخلق والهداية ما تدوم به الحياة ويستمر به نظام الخلق، وهو الغذاء والشرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq retains the first-person yāʾ in يهديني and the following verbs; this is also reported from Nāfiʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.anchor: وأثبت ابن أبي إسحاق ياء المتكلم في يهديني وما بعده، وهي رواية عن نافع.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r1.claim: Under the alternative syntax from the prior verse, this and the next two relative clauses would need omitted predicates supplied from the prior clause, weak in wording and sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r1.anchor: وكذا اللذان بعده ولايخفى ما في ذلك لفظا ومعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r2.claim: The first parsing is more fitting to the Qur'an's eloquence, with this relative clause coordinated to the first one.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r2.anchor: فاللائق بجزالة التنزيل الاعراب الأول وعليه يكون الموصول عطفا على الموصول الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r3.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun marks each set of attributes as independently magnificent and sufficient to warrant worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r3.anchor: للايذان بأن كل واحدة من تلك الصلات نعت جليل له تعالى مستقل في استيجاب الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r4.claim: The apparent sense is that God provides food and drink through other means, unlike creation, which is attributed directly to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r4.anchor: والظأهر أن المراد الاطعام والسقي إلى غيره عز وجل بخلاف الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r5.claim: Al-Warraq gives a mystical reading: God feeds and gives drink without food or drink, like the report that the Prophet spends the night being fed and given drink by his Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r5.anchor: وعن أبي بكر الوراق أن المعنى يطعمني بلا طعام ويسقيني بلا شراب كما جاء أني أبيت يطعمني ربي ويسقين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r6.claim: Food and drink follow creation because they sustain life and the human order and are more persistently needed than other things.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r6.anchor: لما أن دوام الحياة وبقاء نظام خلق الانسان بالغذاء والشراب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r7.claim: Even people in Hell, despite their torment, ask for water and provision, underscoring the need for food and drink.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96/r7.anchor: ألا ترى أن أهل النار وهم في النار لم يشغلهم ماهم فيه من العذاب عن طلبهما فقالوا أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117#2/r6.claim: God provides Abraham with food and drink and is the source of his provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117#2/r6.anchor: أي: يرزقني ويغذني بالطعام والشراب، فهو رازقي ومن عنده رزقي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r5.claim: On the first syntactic analysis, the relative clause about feeding is a subject with an omitted predicate understood from what precedes, as are the two clauses after it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r5.anchor: على الأول مبتدأ محذوف الخبر لدلالة ما قبله عليه وكذا اللذان بعده

SULAMI:v2p75#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r1.speaker: النهرجوري
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r1.claim: God feeds the servant with the sweetness of remembrance and will give him to drink from the cup of His love.
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r1.anchor: قال النهرجوري : الذي اطعمني حلاوة ذكره سيسقيني بكأس محبته

SULAMI:v2p75#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r2.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r2.claim: The feeding is in God's presence; the drink reveals the blessings of that food and drink.
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r2.anchor: قال الجريري : الذي يطعمني في حضرته ، ويسقيني هو الذي يظهر على آثار بركات ذلك المطعم والمشرب

SULAMI:v2p75#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r3.claim: Al-Jurayri cites the Prophet as saying that he spends the night with his Lord, who feeds and gives him drink.
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r3.anchor: لذلك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' إني ابيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقيني '

SULAMI:v2p75#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r4.claim: God revives the soul with the food of service and the spirit with the drink of intimacy.
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : هو الذي يحيي نفسي بطعام الخدمة ، ويحيي روحي بشراب الألفة

SULAMI:v2p75#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r5.claim: God nurtures the servant with His food and gives him life with His drink.
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : هو الذي يربيني بطعامه ويحيني بشرابه

SULAMI:v2p75#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r6.claim: God feeds the servant with the delight of faith and gives him the drink of reliance and sufficiency.
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : يطعمني لذة الايمان ، ويسقيني شراب التوكل والكفاية

SULAMI:v2p75#4/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r7.claim: When divine identity overwhelms the human essence, sensory notions of modality, quantity, and totality dissolve; God feeds the servant with the everlasting food of the righteous, without fatigue.
SULAMI:v2p75#4/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : إذا هجمت بالهوية المعدن تلاشت الكيفية والكمية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r14.claim: God alone provides food and drink; He could remove what Abraham eats and drinks or afflict him so he cannot consume either.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r14.anchor: ولو أراد لأعدم ما آكل وما أشرب أو أصابني بآفة لا أستطيع معها أكلا ولا شربا

TUSTARI:26:79/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:26:79/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:26:79/r1.claim: God feeds Abraham with the delight of faith and gives him the drink of trust and sufficiency.
TUSTARI:26:79/r1.anchor: يطعمني لذة الإيمان، ويسقيني شراب التوكل والكفاية

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq's account says Abraham's mother fled to a cave in labor; Abraham declared that his creator, provider, feeder, and giver of drink was his sole Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق ، فلما وجدت أم إبراهيم الطلق خرجت ليلا إلى مغارة فذكر القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r8.claim: The fronted subject in the food, drink, and healing clauses likewise restricts provision and healing to God against claims that idols arrange sustenance or cure illness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r8.anchor: لِلرد على زعمهم أن الأصنام تقدر لهم تيسير ما يأكلون وما يشربون وبها برؤهم إذا مرضوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun rather than coordinating all clauses directly emphasizes the possessor of these three magnificent divine attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.anchor: وتكرير اسم الموصول في المواضع الثلاثة مع أن مقتضى الظاهر أن تعطف الصلتان على الصلة الأولى للاهتمام بصاحب تلك الصلات الثلاث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.claim: The five divine acts span bodily and intellectual creation, food and water, illness and healing, death, and resurrection; together they trace physical life and the second life as gifts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.anchor: فذكر خلق الجسد وخلق العقل وإعطاء ما به بقاء المخلوق وهو الغذاء والماء ، وما يعتري المرء من اختلال المزاج وشفائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.claim: These descriptions also prepare for spiritual perfection: death looks like a blessing only after reflection, while the life after it is plainly a blessing for whoever wills it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.anchor: وذكر الموت الذي هو خاتمة الحياة الأولى ، وأعقبه بذكر الحياة الثانية للإشارة إلى أن الموت حالة لا يظهر كونها نعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.claim: The first-person yāʾ is omitted from four verbs for lightness and rhyme at pauses, since most endings in this surah use a still nūn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.anchor: وحذفت ياآت المتكلم من { يهدين ، ويسقين ، ويشفين ، ويحيين } لأجل التخفيف ورعاية الفاصلة لأنها يوقف عليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.claim: The paired mention of feeding and giving drink enumerates the blessing of provision.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.anchor: وقوله يطعمني ويسقين تعديد للنعمة في الرزق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.claim: Abū Bakr al-Warrāq, cited by al-Thaʿlabī, says God feeds without food and gives drink without beverage; a Prophetic report says the same.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق في كتاب الثعلبي يطعمني بلا طعام ويسقيني بلا شراب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says that he spends the night with his Lord, who feeds him and gives him drink.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.anchor: كما قال النبي عليه السلام «إني أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقين، وأسند إبراهيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#2/r1.claim: God provides Abraham with food and drink.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r3.claim: God provides through heavenly and earthly means, sending clouds and water, reviving the earth, and producing fruits; He also sends fresh water for livestock and people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r3.anchor: فساق المزن، وأنزل الماء، وأحيا به الأرض، وأخرج به من كل الثمرات رزقا للعباد

NAHHAS:v3p182/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p182/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p182/r11.claim: The yāʾ is omitted at verse endings to keep them uniform; Ibn Abī Isḥāq read all the forms with yāʾ, reasoning that yāʾ is the subject and the nūn entered for a grammatical reason.
NAHHAS:v3p182/r11.anchor: بغير ياء لأن الحذف في رءوس الآيات حسن لتتفق كلها وقد قرأ ابن أبي إسحاق على جلالته ومحله من العربية هذه كلها بالياء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r4.claim: Abraham adduces food, drink, sickness, and healing as proof to his audience because they agree with him about these favors.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.claim: The author rejects speculative interpretations that depart from the apparent meaning and what reason readily accepts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.anchor: تجوز بعض المتعمقة في غوامض المعاني فعدل بذلك عن ظاهره إلى ما تدفعه بداهة العقول

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r8.claim: Some speculative interpreters turn eating and drinking into the pleasure of faith and sweetness of acceptance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r8.anchor: أي يطعمني لذة الإيمان ويسقيني حلاوة القبول

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r9.claim: God feeds Abraham when he is hungry and gives him drink when he is thirsty.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r1.claim: Abraham attributes feeding to the provider of blessings because relying on material causes is characteristic of animals.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r1.anchor: أضاف الإطعام إلى ولى الإنعام لأن لركون إلى الأسباب عادة الأنعام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAta says God gives him life through food and quenches his thirst with drink.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#12/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء هو الذى يحيينى بطعامه ويروينى بشرابه

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r2.claim: The pronoun هو emphasizes that God alone feeds and gives drink; no other does so.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r2.anchor: ودخول { هو } تنبيه على أن غيره لا يطعم ولا يسقي كما تقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r9.speaker: أهل الإشارات
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r9.claim: Esoteric interpreters take feeding and giving drink as imparting the delight of faith and sweetness of acceptance.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r9.anchor: فقال: { والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين } أي يطعمني لذة الإيمان ويسقين حلاوة القبول.

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r9.claim: Food and drink represent every beneficial provision: food alone would not complete the blessing without appetite, strength, and discrimination that enable eating and nourishment.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r9.anchor: من أكله والاغتذاء به نحو الشهوة والقوة

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.claim: Only a being capable of the listed acts is worthy of worship.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.anchor: Only a being capable of the acts listed in these verses is worthy and deserving of worship

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.claim: Symbolically, God nourishes the soul, heals its ailments, and enlivens the spirit by bringing death to the passionate ego.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.anchor: Interpreted symbolically, these verses can mean that God feeds and nourishes the soul, heals the ailments of the soul, and enlivens the spirit

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r4.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r4.claim: Some say the food signifies faith, while the drink signifies trust in God and contentment.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r4.anchor: Others say that the food is faith, and the drink is trust in God and contentment (Su)

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.speaker: Al-Thaʿlabī
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī describes spiritual death and life as justice and grace, disobedience and obedience, separation and meeting God, and ignorance and knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.anchor: Al-Thaʿlabī summarizes the spiritual dimensions of these verses by saying that God brings death through justice and life through grace

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.claim: Others say people die outwardly yet live inwardly, die through forgetting God, and live through remembering Him.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.anchor: one is caused to die outwardly, but is given life inwardly, dies through forgetfulness of God, and lives through remembrance of Him (Su)

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.speaker: Junayd
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.claim: Junayd compares resurrection to nakedness, hunger, and thirst, except for those clothed in reverence and given gnosis and love.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.anchor: Some quote Junayd, who says that when human beings are resurrected on the Day of Judgment

TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r2.claim: God feeds and gives drink to Abraham, providing his sustenance.
TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r2.anchor: والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين} [الشعراء: 79] يقول: والذي يغذوني بالطعام والشراب ويرزقني الأرزاق

SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r1.claim: Alladhī huwa yuṭʿimunī may be a subject with an omitted predicate, as may the following clause, or both may describe the one who created me.
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مبتدأ، وخبره محذوف. وكذلك ما بعده. ويجوز أن يكونوا أوصافا للذي خلقني.

SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r2.claim: Coordination with the waw is permissible; a poetic line illustrates the construction.
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r2.anchor: ودخول الواو جائز. وقد تقدم تحقيقه في أول البقرة كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq, also reportedly followed by ʿĀṣim, retains the first-person yāʾ in yasqīn, yashfīn, and yuḥyīn.
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.anchor: وأثبت ابن أبي إسحاق وتروى عن عاصم أيضا ياء المتكلم في " يسقين " و " يشفين " و " يحيين ".

TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.claim: On the universal reading, feeding, drinking, and healing are particular instances of general guidance; if guidance means religious guidance, these qualities stand separately and guidance precedes other gifts as the best blessing after existence.
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.anchor: من الصفات المعدودة من قبيل ذكر الخاص بعد العام

TABATABAI:26:79-81/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r3.claim: Food, drink, and healing summarize material blessings that supply deficiencies and meet worldly needs, with the most important examples named.
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r3.anchor: هو كالكناية عن جملة النعم المادية التي يرزقه الله إياها لتتميم النواقص ورفع الحوائج الدنيوية

TABATABAI:26:79-81/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r5.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun rather than coordinating these qualities shows that each independently establishes God as Lord, manager, sustainer, and responder to Abraham's prayer.
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r5.anchor: أعاد الموصول فقال { الذي هو يطعمني } الخ، ولم يعطف الصفات

TABRISI:26:78-84/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r4.claim: God provides Abraham's nourishment and drink and keeps his body healthy.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r4.anchor: معناه أنه يرزقني ما أتغذى به ويفعل ما يصح بدني

TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.claim: The final yāʾ letters are omitted because these are verse endings.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.anchor: وإنما حذف الياءات لأنه رؤوس الآيات

TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.claim: Abraham's speech argues against his people that only the one who performs these acts deserves divinity.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.anchor: وهذا الكلام من إبراهيم ع إنما صدر على وجه الاحتجاج على قومه والإخبار بأنه لا يصلح للإلهية إلا من فعل هذه الأفعال.

THALABI:v7p167/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p167/r1.claim: “He feeds and gives me drink” means that God provides for and nurtures Abraham.
THALABI:v7p167/r1.anchor: والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين يعني يرزقني ويربيني

THALABI:v7p167/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r2.speaker: أبو العباس بن عطاء
THALABI:v7p167/r2.claim: Abu al-Abbas ibn ʿAta says God gives Abraham whatever food and drink He wills.
THALABI:v7p167/r2.anchor: وقال أبو العباس بن عطاء: يعني يطعمني أي طعام شاء، ويسقيني أي شراب شاء

THALABI:v7p167/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r3.speaker: محمد بن كثير العبدي
THALABI:v7p167/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kathir al-ʿAbdi reports that Sufyan al-Thawri lived in Mecca and took only a handful of sand by inhaling it from one Sabbath to the next.
THALABI:v7p167/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن كثير العبدي: صحبت سفيان الثوري بمكة دهرا فكان يستف من السبت الى السبت كفا من رمل

THALABI:v7p167/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r4.speaker: راوي خبر إبراهيم بن أدهم
THALABI:v7p167/r4.claim: A visitor seeking Ibrahim ibn Adham found him stoking a kiln; when the visitor wanted food, Ibrahim mixed ash and dirt and ate it, then recited verses urging restraint from asking people for what they possess.
THALABI:v7p167/r4.anchor: خرجت من بلخ في طلب إبراهيم بن أدهم فرأيته بحمص في أتون يسجرها فسلمت عليه وسألته عن حاله

THALABI:v7p167/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r5.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
THALABI:v7p167/r5.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham explains that speech can bring ruin and faults, and advises remembering God when speaking and treating the body as dead when silent.

THALABI:v7p167/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v7p167/r6.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says God can feed and quench without food, drink, or ordinary means; a prophetic report says God feeds and gives drink.
THALABI:v7p167/r6.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق: يطعمني بلا طعام ويسقين بلا شراب، ومجازها: يشبعني ويرويني من غير علاقة

THALABI:v7p167/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p167/r7.claim: A report about a man with a waterskin says he heard the Prophet recite that every creature’s provision is from God, threw away his waterskin, then dreamt of drinking from a cup of Paradise; Anas says he lived over twenty years without customary eating or drinking.
THALABI:v7p167/r7.anchor: حديث السقاء في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة أيام يقرأ وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها

THALABI:v7p167/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p167/r8.speaker: علي بن قادم
THALABI:v7p167/r8.claim: Ali ibn Qadim reports that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nuʿm ate only monthly; Hajjaj confined him for fifteen days, found him praying, and was told that only eaters and drinkers need ablution.
THALABI:v7p167/r8.anchor: وقال علي بن قادم: كان عبد الرحمن بن أبي نعم لا يأكل في الشهر إلا مرة

THALABI:v7p168/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p168/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخزاز
THALABI:v7p168/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khazzaz says that while starving in Tarsus he heard a voice offer him eternal satiety; afterward he had no appetite for years but could eat and drink when he wished.
THALABI:v7p168/r1.anchor: كنت بطرسوس جائعا، فاشتد بي الجوع فجلست على شاطئ النهر ووضعت رجلي في الماء فنوديت

THALABI:v7p168/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p168/r2.speaker: امرأة من حلب
THALABI:v7p168/r2.claim: A woman captured and taken toward the Romans in Sayf al-Dawla’s time escaped and walked two hundred farsakhs without food; she said reciting al-Ikhlas three times when tired or hungry restored strength, food, and drink.
THALABI:v7p168/r2.anchor: وبلغني أن امرأة أسرت من حلب الى الروم في أيام سيف الدولة علي بن حمدان، فهربت منهم ومشت مائتي فرسخ

THALABI:v7p168/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p168/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الشبلي
THALABI:v7p168/r3.claim: Al-Shibli says a subtle property within bread satiates a person, not the bread itself, and God could preserve that property so bread was unnecessary.
THALABI:v7p168/r3.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر الشبلي يقول: في الخبز لطيفة تشبعك لا الخبز، ولو شاء لأبقى فيك تلك اللطيفة حتى لا تحتاج الى الخبز

THALABI:v7p168/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p168/r4.speaker: ذو النون المصري
THALABI:v7p168/r4.claim: Dhu al-Nun says God feeds him the food of love and gives him the drink of love; his poem calls love’s drink the best and all other drink a mirage.
THALABI:v7p168/r4.anchor: وقال ذو النون المصري: يطعمني طعام المحبة ويسقيني شراب المحبة

THALABI:v7p168/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p168/r5.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
THALABI:v7p168/r5.claim: Abu Yazid al-Bistami describes a divine drink of love reserved for devoted servants: it intoxicates and carries them through rapture and ascent to the seat of truth with the Powerful King.
THALABI:v7p168/r5.anchor: إن لله شرابا يقال له شراب المحبة ادخره لأفاضل عباده، فإذا شربوا سكروا

THALABI:v7p168/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p168/r6.speaker: الجنيد
THALABI:v7p168/r6.claim: Al-Junayd says the resurrected are naked except for those clothed in piety, hungry except those who ate knowledge, and thirsty except those who drank love.
THALABI:v7p168/r6.anchor: وقال الجنيد: يحشر الناس كلهم عراة إلا من لبس لباس التقوى، وغراثا إلا من أكل طعام المعرفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p69/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p69/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p69/r1.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the emphatic pronoun huwa indicates that no one besides God feeds and gives drink.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p69/r1.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: صحول {هو} دليل على أنه أعلم أنه لا يطعم ولا يسقي غيره

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r4.claim: God provides Abraham's food and drink.

DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet promises guidance, Paradise food and drink, healing and expiation, blessed life and martyrdom, forgiveness, wisdom, truthful renown, and Paradise homes for one who recites Abraham’s prayer after ablution while leaving for obligatory prayer; al-Ḥasan adds a prayer for the parents.
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا توضأ العبد لصلاة مكتوبة فاسبغ الوضوء

BURHAN:v2p142/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p142/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p142/r4.claim: The Prophet's statement that he stays with his Lord, who feeds and gives him drink, echoes Abraham: God's special servants are nourished through glorification, declaration of divine unity, and praise rather than food.
BURHAN:v2p142/r4.anchor: إنى أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقين فى معنى قوله حكاية عن خليله ﴿ والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين ﴾

BURHAN:v4p68/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p68/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p68/r4.claim: The present tense marks repeatedly renewed feeding and drinking; waw is used because the people did not distinguish the feeder from the provider of drink, while هو clarifies the source.
BURHAN:v4p68/r4.anchor: فاتى بالمضارع لبيان تجدد الاطعام والسقيا وجاءت الواو دون الفاء لانهم كانوا لايفرقون بين المطعم والساقي

ITQAN:v3p293/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.claim: Al-Tibi says Abraham’s speech combines a graceful transition and a good request: he moves from God’s attributes to “My Lord, grant me judgment and join me with the righteous.”
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.anchor: قال الطيبي ومما اجتمع فيه حسن التخلص والمطلب معا قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم

ITQAN:v3p240/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.claim: Al-Tafwit is presenting varied meanings, such as praise and description, in separate sentences of equal measure; it may use long, medium, or short sentences.
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.anchor: هو إتيان المتكلم بمعان شتى من المدح والوصف وغير ذلك من الفنون كل فن في جملة منفصلة

ITQAN:v3p240/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.claim: Abraham's successive statements about God's guidance, provision, healing, death, and revival exemplify al-tafwit in long sentences.
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.anchor: فمن الطويلة ﴿ الذي خلقني فهو يهدين والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين

ITQAN:v3p244/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p244/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p244/r7.claim: Muṣaḥḥaf, also called line jinās, pairs words whose letters differ by dotting, as in the cited verbs.
ITQAN:v3p244/r7.anchor: ومنها المصحف ويسمى جناس الخط بأن تختلف الحروف في النقط كقوله ﴿ والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين وإذا مرضت فهو يشفين ﴾

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.claim: Abraham attributes creation, guidance, food, drink, and healing to God, but says ‘when I am ill’ rather than ascribing illness to God.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه نسب الخير إلى ربه

NASHR:v2p336/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p336/r10.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p336/r10.claim: Yaqub affirms the sixteen listed extra yāʾs in both connected and pause forms: the eight quoted forms plus أطيعون in eight places.
NASHR:v2p336/r10.anchor: أثبت الياء في جميعها يعقوب في الحالين
